title: G. Many Cartesian Trees
statement:
Consider an array a consisting of n distinct integers. The Cartesian Tree of a is defined as a unique binary tree^{∗} that satisfies the following conditions:

Denote r(a) as the root of the Cartesian Tree, and f_a(i) as the parent of i in the Cartesian Tree.

Define E_a={(i,f_a(i)) mid 1 ≤ i ≤ n, i ≠ r(a)}.

Consider a permutation^{§} q of length n. We define a series of arrays p_1,p_2,…,p_n as follows:

You are now given n and S=bigcuplimits_{i=1}^n E_p_i. To minimize input, S will be given in the form of a n × n binary matrix s. Denote s_{i,j} as the j-th character of the i-th row. s_{i,j}=1 if and only if (i,j) ∈ S.

Please find any permutation q such that S can be obtained by the process above. It is guaranteed that the tests are generated to ensure a valid q always exists.

^{∗}A binary tree is a rooted tree, in which each node has no more than 2 children, referred to as the left child and the right child.

^{†}The parent of vertex v is the first vertex on the simple path from v to the root. The root has no parent.

^{‡}A subtree of vertex v is the subgraph of v, all its descendants, and all the edges between them.

^{§}A permutation of length n is an array consisting of n distinct integers from 1 to n in arbitrary order. For example, [2,3,1,5,4] is a permutation, but [1,2,2] is not a permutation (2 appears twice in the array), and [1,3,4] is also not a permutation (n=3 but there is 4 in the array).

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^4). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test contains an integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 3000) — the length of q that you need to find.

The i-th of the next n lines contains a binary string of length n, representing the i-th row of s. It is guaranteed that s_{i,i} = 0 for all 1 ≤ i ≤ n.

It is guaranteed that the tests are generated to ensure a valid q always exists.

It is guaranteed that the sum of n^2 over all test cases does not exceed 9·10^6.

For each test case, output n integers q_1,q_2,…,q_n, representing the permutation q you found.

Input:
```
320110301110001040101001010010110
```

Output:
```
1 22 1 33 1 2 4
```
